outcome: length of the latent phase of labor
length of the active phase of labor
total first stage of labor duration
cohort: The study included 41,868 patients who underwent vaginal delivery of singleton, cephalic-presenting fetuses at >=37 weeks of gestation, with at least 2 documented cervical examinations between 2- and 10-cm dilations, at a large, tertiary hospital in New York City.
finding: Higher maternal body mass index was associated with slower labor progress and longer labor duration, primarily driven by longer times spent in the latent phase of labor, with no significant difference observed in the active phase.
